title: A simple, low cost GC/MS method for the sub-nanogram per litre measurement of organotins in coastal water
author: Cole, Mills, et al.

steps.title: Observe safety precautions
steps.instruction: Handle organotin compounds and NaBEt4 in a fume hood with a carbon filter, purchase only ~1 g of NaBEt4 to minimise exposure, and dispose waste stock standards as chlorinated organotin waste.

steps.title: Clean glassware
steps.instruction: Wash glassware with 10 % Decon‑90 solution at 85 °C, soak in 12 M HCl for 24 h, rinse sequentially with water then methanol, and dry at 60 °C.

steps.title: Prepare standards and samples
steps.instruction: In a labelled 250 mL volumetric flask add 20 µL internal standard (TPrT, 1.0 mg L⁻¹) and the required volume of calibration standard, then add deionised or coastal water using a glass funnel up to the mark.

steps.title: Add n‑hexane and mix
steps.instruction: Add 2.0 mL n‑hexane to the flask and shake by hand for approximately 1 min to mix the two phases.

steps.title: Mechanical shaking
steps.instruction: Place the flask on a mechanical shaker for 15 min at 400 oscillations min⁻¹.

steps.title: Separate phases and add buffer
steps.instruction: Allow the n‑hexane/water phases to separate for about 5 min, then add 1.0 mL sodium acetate buffer solution and invert the flask to mix.

steps.title: Add NaBEt4 and ethylate
steps.instruction: In a fume hood add 1 % NaBEt4 (1.0 mL) to the flask, stopper, shake manually for 1 min, then place on the shaker for 10 min at 400 oscillations min⁻¹ to ethylate the organotin compounds.

steps.title: Dry extract and transfer
steps.instruction: Allow layers to separate for ~30 min, carefully transfer the n‑hexane layer to a 10 mL glass vial, add ~4 g anhydrous sodium sulphate, seal with a foil‑lined cap and shake to remove residual water, then transfer the extract to an amber 2 mL vial for instrumental analysis.

steps.title: Store extracts if needed
steps.instruction: If not analysed immediately, store derivatised extracts at –20 °C in the dark for no longer than 1 week.
